Tom — thanks for the alert and the traces. Sorry you're hit with this right before the demo. We're looking at it now.

Quick answers up front:
- Immediate mitigation (client): enforce exponential backoff and jitter for retries (we'll send a suggested patch snippet). Also please disable aggressive reconnects — a single reconnect per session with 5s jitter is preferable to continuous floods.
- Short-term server tweak (Redwood): we can increase the idle keepalive window for your VPC routing layer and add an interim server-side grace for in-flight KV cache reads to avoid spurious 5xx. That requires a short deploy.
- Longer-term: root cause appears related to intermediate network/load-balancer idle timeouts + our streaming keepalive behavior; we'll run a canary of a keepalive ping approach.

I'm escalating to our infra and on-call. Looping in Lauren for customer comms and Karthik for tech triage.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Adding technical notes from initial triage:
- Edge logs: confirmed multiple RST_STREAM events originating from our side of the edge LB. Timestamp correlation shows RSTs coincide with rapid burst of concurrent reconnects from same client IP ranges.
- Root cause hypothesis: combination of (a) intermediate infra (customer side LB + our edge) having default idle TCP/HTTP/2 timeouts ~30s, and (b) our streaming code doesn't emit frequent application-level keepalives for low-throughput sessions, so the connection is perceived as idle and torn down. When client retries without backoff, the edge sees a sudden spike, saturates upstream worker pools, and returns 429/502/504 depending on where the request fails.
- Short-term mitigations we can push within 60–90 minutes:
  * Increase HTTP/2 keepalive timeout on the edge from 30s -> 90s for Acme's routing rule (config toggle, no build).
  * Add a server-side 1s application-level ping for streaming sessions in the next hotfix (deploy to canary in us-west).
  * Throttle rapid reconnects at our edge by applying a per-source-token 10 req/s burst limiter and queue smoothing (config-only change).
- Customer-side mitigations we recommend:
  * Implement exponential backoff with min 1s, max 10s, jitter.
  * Hold open long polls for at least 60s before reconnecting.

I'll prepare the config changes and start the canary. Will post the patch diff to the incident link.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@acmehealth.com>, sre@acmehealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Acme Health — interim mitigations deployed, next steps

Tom — quick update from our side after the triage and canary run. Summary of actions completed:
- We increased the edge HTTP/2 idle timeout for Acme's routing rule to 90s (config change) around 11:20 PT on 2026-11-18.
- Deployed an application-level streaming ping to canary (us-west) that sends a 1s keepalive when a stream is otherwise idle; canary showed a 72% reduction in RST_STREAM and 60% fewer total retries in test traffic.
- Applied a per-token rate-limiter to smooth reconnect bursts to 10 req/s with queue smoothing to prevent immediate 429 spikes.

Customer asks fulfilled:
1) Mitigation you can apply right now: add exponential backoff + jitter and limit reconnects to 1 reconnect per session with 5–10s jitter. We attached a client patch snippet (see related_links).
2) Suggested Redwood config: we recommend leaving the edge idle timeout at 90s for at least 72 hours while we monitor.
3) Permanent fix plan: we will roll the streaming ping to additional regions after validation, and instrument a fallback that proxies small pings at the edge to keep h2 connections healthy. Estimated full rollout: 48–72 hours.

Follow-ups:
- Karthik will post metrics on the incident page and we'll keep logs for your team to validate.
- Lauren will send a short postmortem after the rollout completes.

Apologies again for the disruption — please let us know if you see any further issues; we'll keep monitoring and can pause the rollout if anything regresses.
